NCO Config & QRZ Link

This callsign is highlighted in red on the master roster, current session list, and map. The NCO map dot uses the coordinates below.
QRZ: Not logged in
Use Login to test QRZ credentials and confirm the current proxy route works. Save Configuration stores the settings.
After your first login attempt this is enabled by default. When QRZ drops, the tool will retry login until the connection returns.
Retry interval controls how often automatic relogin attempts happen. Request timeout controls how long each login attempt may wait.
Health checks verify QRZ periodically. If disabled, the app only changes QRZ status during login and lookups.
RAW remains the default. If RAW is unreliable, try CorsProxy.io. JSON is left as a last-resort fallback because it is usually less reliable for this tool.
Timeout controls how long each QRZ proxy request may wait. Delay controls the pause between QRZ lookups and retries, which can reduce bottlenecks.
Use this button after changing proxy, timeout, retry, health check, or cooldown values. The auto-relogin loop immediately uses the new saved settings.

Data Import / Export

Export a backup before making major changes. Import replaces the current browser Master Roster with the selected JSON file.

Wipe Master Roster / Transcript

Warning: These actions are separate. Wiping the Master Roster removes saved operators, roster history, comments, notes, locations, and the current session checklist. Wiping transcripts removes only the permanent transcript archive. Factory reset removes everything and returns the tool to first-run defaults. There is no turning back unless you exported a backup first.

Overview

The Net Control Tool is a single-file HTML program for managing an amateur radio net. It helps you check in stations, maintain a master roster, track the current session, save signal reports, record weather and message traffic, manage UTC timing, view station maps, check propagation, print tactical reports, and preserve participation history.

The program runs entirely from one HTML file and saves information locally in your browser.

Starting the Program

  1. Open the HTML file in Chrome, Edge, or Firefox.
  2. Use the same browser and computer to keep the same saved Master Roster.
  3. Use Export and Import in Settings if you need to move the Master Roster to another computer.

Main Screen Layout

The left pane contains the Roster, Map, Repeaters, Regular Check In's, Propagation, and Transcript tabs. The top bar includes a separate Help button.

The right pane contains the Current Session Checklist, where active check-ins are managed.

The top bar contains Tools, Online/Offline mode, ID timer, Print Tactical PDF, Clear Current Session, Sync New QRZ, and Settings.

Settings

Click Settings in the top bar to configure the program.

  • QRZ username and password
  • Net Controller Station
  • NCO latitude and longitude
  • Frequency and mode
  • ID timer settings
  • Map distance-line settings
  • Mobile station behavior
  • Session summary printing
  • Import, export, full sync, and Master Roster wipe

QRZ Setup and Sync

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Enter your QRZ username and password.
  3. Click Save Configuration.

If successful, the background log will show QRZ authentication succeeded.

Sync New QRZ

The top Sync New QRZ button only searches stations that have not already been synced. This helps avoid bottlenecks during a live net.

FULL Master Roster Sync

Full Master Roster Sync is inside Settings. It refreshes every station in the Master Roster and may overwrite manually entered profile data with QRZ data.

Net Controller Station

The Net Controller Station setting identifies the station running the net.

  • The NCO callsign appears next to the Current Session Checklist title.
  • The NCO is highlighted in red in the roster and current session.
  • The NCO appears as a large red dot on the map.
  • Distance lines can be drawn from the NCO to known stations.

NCO Coordinates

Set the NCO latitude and longitude in decimal format inside Settings. These coordinates are used for distance, bearing, map lines, the offline distance grid, and tactical reports.

Example: Latitude: 33.4655 and Longitude: -112.0736.

Frequency and Mode

Frequency and mode are configured in Settings and saved with the session archive.

Examples: 146.520 MHz / FM, 7.268 MHz / LSB, or 147.240+ / FM.

Adding Stations to the Current Session

  1. Type a callsign into the input box on the right pane.
  2. Press Enter.
  3. The callsign is added to the Current Session Checklist.

If the station already exists in the Master Roster, saved information is loaded immediately. If the callsign is new, QRZ lookup may populate the profile when online.

Current Session Card Controls

  • Check-in checkbox: marks the station checked or completed.
  • Mobile checkbox: marks the station mobile and, by default, moves it to the top.
  • Move up/down: changes the station order.
  • Remove: removes the station from the current session only.
  • Emergency traffic: highlights emergency traffic and includes it on reports.
  • Speech bubble: opens the station comment or memo editor.
  • Pencil: opens manual profile editing.
  • QRZ link: opens the station profile on QRZ.

Saving Station Reports

Each station card includes RST, weather, and traffic/message fields. Click Save Card after entering the report.

When saved, the row greys out, the fields become read-only, and the button changes to Edit Card. Click Edit Card to unlock and revise the report.

The Master Roster shows the latest saved report, including signal report, weather report, and traffic message.

UTC Start and End Times for Each Station

Only the next active station shows live ticking UTC start and end clocks. This avoids a screen full of moving clocks.

  • Check Start UTC when the station begins speaking.
  • Check End UTC when the station finishes.
  • Times include seconds, such as 21:14:37Z.
  • When both times are locked, the row collapses to a small read-only summary.
  • Use the pencil icon to manually edit locked times.

Session Clock

Click the clock emoji next to Current Session Checklist to open the session clock.

The session clock has Session Start UTC and Session End UTC. Checking Start UTC locks only the start time. End UTC continues ticking until its own box is checked.

Session times are saved indefinitely and appear on tactical PDF reports.

Session Summary

Click the notepad emoji next to the session clock to open the Session Summary editor.

Use it to record net purpose, number of check-ins, emergency traffic, frequency changes, band conditions, training notes, and closing comments.

When Session End UTC is checked, the program reminds the net controller to add a session summary. In Settings, the summary can be printed as its own final page.

Master Roster

The Master Roster is the permanent station Master Roster. It stores callsign, name, license/profile type, address or QTH, coordinates, first seen date, total check-in days, saved reports, comments, and history.

Net history is shown in a compact format like [First Seen: 05/01/2026 total 82 Days].

New stations show a small green *New label.

Manual Profile Editing

Use the pencil icon to manually edit a station profile. You can enter name, license/profile type, address/QTH, latitude, and longitude.

This is useful when QRZ is unavailable, the station is not found, or the station needs coordinates for the map. A Full Master Roster Sync may overwrite manual data with QRZ data later.

Online and Offline Mode

Online mode attempts QRZ lookups and online map tiles. Offline mode relies on local saved data and manual entry.

Previously saved stations populate from the Master Roster even without internet access.

Map Tab

The Map tab displays stations with saved latitude and longitude and optional repeater markers.

Filters include Current Session, Today’s Visitors, This Week, Last 30 Days, and All Operators.

  • Use the callsign search box to quickly focus a roster station on the map.
  • The NCO is shown as a large red dot.
  • Station pins appear for stations with saved coordinates.
  • Repeater markers appear as 📡 icons when the map is set to Stations + Repeaters or Repeaters Only.
  • Repeater display is filtered by one saved state/region/country at a time so the map is not flooded.
  • Distance lines can be enabled directly on the Map tab or in Settings.
  • Hovering over distance lines shows range and bearing.
  • The offline distance grid plots stations by distance and bearing from the NCO.

Repeater Tab

The Repeater tab stores a local repeater list. On a fresh first run, the tool starts with the ARA Frequency List dated 2023-11-29 as a starter set. After the first run, those repeaters are just normal local repeater records, so you can edit them, delete them, export selected entries to CHIRP, import CHIRP CSV files, or add your own repeaters without the tool forcing them back in.

Repeaters with coordinates can be shown on the Map tab as 📡 markers. Clicking a repeater marker shows connection information so net control can help a station move to or use that repeater.

The Repeater tab can also export saved repeaters into a CHIRP-style CSV file. Select individual repeaters to export only those, or leave nothing selected to export everything currently displayed in the list. You can also select displayed repeaters and delete them in bulk. The export uses the locally saved repeater records and does not require an online repeater database connection.

The Address Lookup button can attempt a light OpenStreetMap/Nominatim geocode for the entered location, but manual latitude and longitude are recommended for reliable placement.

Printing the Map

Use Print Map in the Map tab to print only the map. It hides the header, roster, current session, settings, tools, and side controls.

Propagation Tab

The Propagation tab displays solar-terrestrial data from HamQSL. This panel requires internet access to refresh.

Tools Menu

  • Script: editable saved net script for opening, closing, emergency nets, training, or announcements.
  • US Call Map: zoomable U.S. call district map.

ID Timer

The ID timer reminds the net controller when to identify. It can be enabled, disabled, and adjusted in Settings. When the timer expires, the program alerts the net controller.

Tactical PDF Report

Click Print Tactical PDF to generate a print-ready report. Use your browser print dialog to print or save as PDF.

The report can include date, NCO station, NCO coordinates, frequency, mode, session start/end UTC, check-in order, callsign, operator details, address/QTH, range and bearing, mobile status, emergency status, RST, weather, traffic message, individual station start/end UTC, and optional session summary page.

Import and Export

Import and Export are located in Settings.

  • Export Data: downloads a JSON backup of your saved Master Roster.
  • Import Data: restores a previously exported JSON backup.

Export regularly if the roster and history are important.

Clearing the Current Session

The visible Clear Current Session button clears only the active checklist. It does not delete the Master Roster.

Wiping the Master Roster

The wipe Master Roster option is located in Settings to prevent accidental deletion. It removes everything from the saved browser Master Roster and cannot be undone unless you have an exported backup.

Recommended Workflow

Before the Net

  1. Open the HTML file.
  2. Confirm Net Controller Station and NCO coordinates.
  3. Confirm frequency and mode in Settings.
  4. Authenticate QRZ if online.
  5. Start the session clock.
  6. Open your script if needed.
  7. Enable the ID timer if desired.

During Roll Call

  1. Type each callsign and press Enter.
  2. Mark mobile stations when needed.
  3. Save signal reports, weather, and traffic.
  4. Use UTC start and end times for each active station.
  5. Mark emergency traffic when applicable.
  6. Use the map to view station locations.

Ending the Net

  1. Lock the Session End UTC time.
  2. Complete the session summary.
  3. Print or save the tactical PDF report.
  4. Export a backup if needed.
  5. Clear the Current Session when ready.

Best Practices

  • Export your Master Roster regularly.
  • Use Sync New QRZ during active nets.
  • Use Full Master Roster Sync only when you want a full refresh.
  • Enter manual latitude and longitude for stations you want on the map.
  • Keep NCO coordinates accurate for distance and bearing.
  • Complete the session summary before printing final reports.
  • Do not wipe the Master Roster unless you have a backup.
  • Save each station card after entering report details.
